title: Given knowledge, their first words were praise.
subtitle: How Dawud and Sulayman received a gift
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah gave Dawud and his son Sulayman {reward}power and authority in this world, and the position of Prophets.{/reward} Their reaction was praise. The surah introduction contrasts this with the Makkan chiefs, who had far less and were full of vanity.
now: You get the promotion. The exam result comes back high. The baby sleeps through the night. {idea}What comes out of your mouth first?{/idea} Dawud and Sulayman had far more and started with al-hamdu lillah.
old: When something good happens, it is mostly because I worked for it.
new: The first right response to any gift is to thank the One who gave it.
try: The next good news you get today, say al-hamdu lillah before telling anyone.

title: He inherited a mission, not a fortune.
subtitle: Sulayman, the birds, and evident bounty
then: Ibn Kathir explains Sulayman inherited {idea}kingship and prophethood, not wealth{/idea}, citing the Prophet ﷺ: "We Prophets cannot be inherited from; whatever we leave behind is charity." Sulayman understood birds and animals, and he called it {reward}clearly the blessings of Allah upon us.{/reward}
now: Your father left you a small shop, or a name people respect, or just his habit of praying at the masjid. {idea}The most valuable inheritance is rarely in the will.{/idea} And when you tell people what you have, the way you describe it shows who you credit.
old: What I inherit is measured by money and property.
new: The best inheritance is faith and responsibility, and every gift is Allah's bounty.
try: Name one good thing a parent or elder passed to you that is not money. Thank Allah for it.

title: A vast army, every one in its place.
subtitle: Sulayman's hosts of jinn, men and birds
then: Ibn Kathir describes Sulayman riding in a display of might, men behind him, then jinn, and {reward}birds shading him with their wings when it was hot.{/reward} Mujahid said officials kept each group in order {idea}so no one would step out of line.{/idea}
now: You lead a team, a household, a class, a WhatsApp group of cousins. The temptation is to act big. {idea}Real strength looks like order: everyone knows their place and no one gets lost.{/idea}
old: Having power means people notice me.
new: Power given by Allah is a trust to organize and look after people well.
try: Check on one person under your care today who might be falling out of line or left behind.

title: One small ant warned her whole valley.
subtitle: The ant who gave the surah its name

row.title: being crushed
sub: by those who do not notice

key.label: How she spoke of the army

then: The surah takes its name from this valley of the ants. As Sulayman's army crossed it, {idea}one ant called out to the others to go into their dwellings{/idea} so they would not be crushed. She added that Sulayman and his soldiers {idea}would not even perceive it.{/idea}
now: You see the scam message going around the family chat and you are the one who types: do not click this. {idea}One small voice can protect a whole group.{/idea} And you can warn without making anyone the villain.
old: I am too small for my warning to matter.
new: One small voice, used early and fairly, can save many.
try: Share one honest, useful warning with someone who needs it today, gently.

title: He smiled at an ant, then asked to be grateful.
subtitle: Sulayman's prayer for gratitude and good deeds
then: Sulayman understood the ant and {reward}smiled, amused.{/reward} Ibn Kathir explains his prayer: inspire me to give thanks for understanding the birds and animals, and for making my parents believers. Then {idea}join me with the righteous when I die.{/idea}
now: Your toddler says something funny, your colleague shares a small kindness. You smile. {idea}That smile is a door.{/idea} Sulayman turned his into a prayer to be grateful, to do good, and to end among good people.
old: Being grateful is something I can just decide to feel.
new: Even gratitude is a gift I ask Allah for, and it should include my parents.
try: Learn the first line of Sulayman's prayer, rabbi awzi'ni, and say it once tonight.

title: A king who noticed one missing bird.
subtitle: Sulayman checks on the hoopoe

row.title: is he absent?
sub: or do I not see him

then: Ibn Abbas and others said the hoopoe had a special skill: {reward}he could tell Sulayman where water lay under open land{/reward}, and how deep. One day Sulayman checked on the birds and could not see him. He first asked if the fault was in his own sight.
now: The quiet kid at the back of the class. The cousin who stopped showing up to Eid. The colleague who has gone silent on calls. {idea}Noticing who is missing is a kind of care.{/idea}
old: If someone drifts away, they will reach out if they need me.
new: Caring for people includes noticing who is not there.
try: Message one person you have not heard from in a while. Just ask how they are.

title: A firm warning, with an exception left open.
subtitle: Unless he brings a clear reason
then: Sulayman spoke strongly about the absent hoopoe, but added: {idea}unless he brings me a clear reason.{/idea} Sufyan bin Uyaynah and Abdullah bin Shaddad report that when the hoopoe returned and heard there was an exception, he said, {reward}then I am saved.{/reward}
now: Your teenager comes home two hours late. Your employee missed the deadline. {idea}You can be firm and still leave room for their reason.{/idea} That word unless is the difference between justice and anger.
old: When someone lets me down, I have every right to judge them straight away.
new: Being firm is fair only when I leave space to hear their reason.
try: Next time someone lets you down today, ask what happened before you react.

title: A small bird told a prophet something new.
subtitle: The hoopoe returns from Sheba
then: The hoopoe was not gone long. He told Sulayman: {idea}I have come to know something that you and your troops do not know.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says Saba refers to Himyar, a dynasty in Yemen, and the news was true and certain.
now: The intern spots the error in your slides. Your kid shows you how to fix the phone setting. {idea}Knowledge does not care about rank.{/idea} Sulayman, prophet and king, listened to a bird.
old: People below me have little to teach me.
new: The smallest person in the room may know exactly what I am missing.
try: Ask someone younger or junior to you for their view on something today, and listen.

title: A queen with everything and a great throne.
subtitle: The hoopoe describes the ruler of Sheba
then: Al-Hasan Al-Basri said this was Bilqis, queen of Saba. Ibn Kathir says she had {reward}all the conveniences a powerful monarch could need{/reward} and a throne adorned with gold, jewels and pearls. The surah introduction notes her wealth far exceeded that of the Quraysh.
now: You scroll past the house tours, the holiday photos, the big wedding. It looks like they have everything. {idea}Having everything still leaves the most important question open.{/idea} The next verse asks it.
old: People who have everything must have life figured out.
new: Wealth and power tell me what someone has, not where their heart is turned.
try: When you feel envy today, ask yourself what you would want more than their things.

title: Bowing to the sun instead of its Maker.
subtitle: The hoopoe sees the people of Sheba
then: Historians described her palace with windows the sun shone through as it rose and set, and {trap}the people prostrated to the sun morning and evening.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains Shaytan made their deeds look good and kept them from the way of truth.
now: You do not bow to the sun. But what lights up your day? The salary, the likes, the approval of one person. {trap}Whatever you arrange your mornings and evenings around starts to act like a god.{/trap}
old: Worshipping things is something only ancient people did.
new: I can turn my whole day toward something bright that Allah made and forget Him.
try: Notice the first thing you reach for when you wake. Put a short dhikr before it tomorrow.

title: He brings out what is hidden, and knows yours.
subtitle: Why prostration belongs to Allah
then: The hoopoe explains why they should bow to Allah. Ibn Abbas said He {idea}knows everything hidden in the heavens and the earth.{/idea} Ibn Kathir adds He knows what His servants say and do in secret and in the open, both the same to Him.
now: Your search history. The message you deleted. The thought you had during the meeting. The quiet good you did that nobody saw. {idea}All of it is open to Him.{/idea} That is a warning and a comfort at once.
old: What I do in private stays private.
new: Allah knows my hidden side, both the faults and the quiet good.
try: Do one good deed today that no one will ever know about.

title: Her throne was great. His Throne is greater.
subtitle: The hoopoe ends with tawhid
then: The hoopoe had just described the queen's great throne. Now he says Allah is {idea}Lord of the Supreme Throne, and there is none greater than Him in all of creation.{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes the hoopoe was calling to good, and cites a hadith in which the Prophet ﷺ forbade killing hoopoes.
now: The CEO's office. The mansion on the hill. The stage at the conference. {idea}They feel huge when you stand in front of them.{/idea} Next to the Lord of the Great Throne, every earthly throne is small.
old: Powerful people and big institutions are the biggest things in my world.
new: Every throne I am impressed by is tiny next to the Throne of Allah.
try: Before a meeting or call that intimidates you, say la ilaha illa Allah once, slowly.

title: Good news or not, check it first.
subtitle: Sulayman tests the hoopoe's report
then: Sulayman did not dismiss the hoopoe or accept him blindly. Ibn Kathir explains he wondered whether the bird was telling the truth, or {trap}lying to save himself from the threat.{/trap} So he said: {idea}we shall see.{/idea}
now: A screenshot lands in the family group: shocking news about someone you know. Your thumb is already on forward. {idea}We will see is a powerful sentence.{/idea} Check it before you pass it on.
old: If news comes from someone I trust, I can share it straight away.
new: Even trusted sources get checked before I act on what they say.
try: Before forwarding the next message today, check whether it is true.

title: Deliver the letter, step back, and watch.
subtitle: Sulayman sends the hoopoe to Sheba
then: Sulayman wrote a letter and told the hoopoe to deliver it and draw back. Ibn Kathir says the bird threw it through a small window into her chamber, then {idea}stepped to one side out of good manners{/idea} to see what they would do.
now: You finally send the honest email to your brother, or share the reminder with a friend. Then you refresh every two minutes. {idea}Deliver it well, then step back.{/idea} Give them room to answer.
old: After I say something important, I have to keep pushing until they respond.
new: My job is to deliver the message with good manners, then give space.
try: Send one message you have been holding back, then put your phone away for an hour.
